title: Stories Written in Stone
question: What counts as a fossil, and how have people made sense of them?
hook: Neanderthals set fossils into the grips of stone knives, and ancient Egyptians kept fossil bones in their temples.
idea: Fossils are the preserved remains, impressions or traces of past life, and people have collected and explained them since at least the start of recorded history.

beats.prompt: Sort each find into its kind of fossil.
beats.explain: Body fossils preserve part of the organism itself, usually its partly mineralized parts; trace fossils are marks it left while alive, like tracks or feces.

beats.prompt: Match each fossil to what people once took it to be.
pairs: Relics kept in temples of Set
beats.explain: Many cultures folded fossils into their beliefs, reading them as parts of gods or mythical creatures.

beats.prompt: Aristotle notices that seashells inside rocks look just like shells on a beach. What does he conclude?

choices.label: The fossils were once living animals
They formed from vapors in the rock
choices.feedback: That was his earlier explanation, which he moved away from after the comparison.

choices.label: People carved them as decorations
choices.feedback: The match with real beach shells pointed to living animals, not to carving.

beats.explain: Seeing that fossil shells resembled beach shells, Aristotle realized the fossils had once been living animals.

beats.prompt: Put these steps in understanding fossils in time order.
items: Shen Kuo links mountain sea fossils to an old seashore
Albert of Saxony builds on fossil shells coming from the sea
Fossils are tied to particular rock layers
Radiometric dating gives fossils absolute ages
beats.explain: Shen Kuo wrote in 1088, Albert of Saxony in the 14th century, the link to rock strata came in the 19th century and radiometric dating in the early 20th.
